rootCause: Actual CSharp mouse next decrements active-next before its remaining event access. Concurrent drop sees zero and closes/frees context; next then signals the closed event. Actual generated functions reproduce both value and closed return paths. Native SLG lacks the active-reader guard entirely. Join drop currently calls input destructors before joining its pulling workers, leaving a callback-entry gap as well.
scope: Actual CSharp next/drop bodies from a successful public compile. Deterministic legal retirement schedule and OS/allocation stubs; no real console, OS-thread safety or full platform qualification claim.

relatedSourceFindings.evidence: CSharp EmitStreamJoinDropCallback calls runtime_cancel, input DropOwnedRuntimeValue, then runtime_join_destroy. Shared worker sets pulling before invoking pull; cancellation settlement is not callback-entry lifetime ownership.
Windows single CancelSynchronousIo followed by infinite join can race before the worker enters ReadConsoleInputW. Official docs describe cancellation of current pending operations, not later calls.
